command: grep -rl -iE 'yank' docs/ release-checklists/ CHANGELOG.md README.md | while read f; do grep -iE 'yank' "$f" | grep -viqE 'yanked (numpy|upstream)' && echo "$f"; done | wc -l
note: CORRECTED after audit. The first measurement counted 5 files matching /yank/, but 2 of those matched an unrelated dependency advisory ('the declared numpy floor 2.4.0 is yanked upstream') rather than mixle's rollback policy. Filtering that out leaves 3. Documented policy, not a machine gate: nothing enforces it at publish time and nothing can -- it governs what a human does after a bad release.
result: 3 documents state the yank-not-delete rollback policy: release-checklists/0.8.0.md, 0.7.0.md and README.md
